name: AEK Athens

C.evidence: Original 21 at Gate 21 are among Greece's most intense ultras; 'well over 1 million' fans. OPAP Arena (Agia Sophia, 32,500) opened 2022 on the Nikos Goumas site: elite atmosphere (9) with the new-stadium -1.

V.evidence: Main shirt sponsor Pame Stoixima (OPAP sports betting) lowers; Original 21's anti-fascist/left identity and the refugee (Constantinople) roots offset. Net typical.

H.evidence: 14 Greek titles, 16 cups; first Greek club in a European Cup QF (1968-69) and UEFA Cup SF (1977). Relegated 2013 and rebuilt from the third tier.

O.evidence: Owned by Marios Iliopoulos (Greek shipping businessman) since 2015; financed the new stadium and rebuilt the club after 2013. Private owner, acceptable conduct.

S.evidence: Competitive Greek champion (2023, 2026); energetic but not a defined high-press identity.

flags: Greek football violence context: AEK fans involved in the 2013 pitch invasion (points deduction). The 2023 killing of an AEK fan was by Dinamo Zagreb ultras (victims, not perpetrators). No violence adjustment applied; confirm.

name: Atlético Madrid

C.evidence: Loud, loyal support; ~70,800 Metropolitano since 2017 (move now 9 seasons old, no new-stadium drop). Lost the character of the Calderón; Frente Atlético-led south stand drives the noise.

V.evidence: Riyadh Air (Saudi PIF-owned state airline) is main shirt sponsor and stadium name (Riyadh Air Metropolitano, ~EUR300m): authoritarian-state sponsor. Frente Atlético has far-right roots; 2023 Vinícius effigy (four ultras convicted as hate crime 2025).

H.evidence: 11 La Liga titles, 3 Europa Leagues, European Cup finals 1974, 2014, 2016; Madrid's working-class counterweight to Real.

O.evidence: Apollo Sports Capital (PE) became 55% majority owner in March 2026; Quantum Pacific ~25%. Gil/Cerezo remain in charge (controversial 1990s conversion to SAD).

S.evidence: Simeone era (since 2011) built on intensity, work rate and collective effort; less defensive recently but still a running identity.

adjustments.evidence: Apollo Sports Capital (private-equity sports fund) majority shareholder since March 2026.
UEFA fined the club EUR30,000 for fans' racist behaviour at Benfica (Oct 2024); nine fans banned for life for racism (2024); Frente Atlético ultras convicted over the Vinícius effigy.
Sept 2024 derby suspended after objects thrown from the Frente's stand (partial closure); history includes the 2014 killing of a Deportivo fan in a pre-arranged clash involving Frente.
2021 Super League founder; withdrew within days.

flags: Racism+violence total -14 vs old -10 combined; check scale vs Lazio -30.
Apollo: consider whether -6 PE or harsher if any acquisition debt is loaded on the club (not found).

name: Barcelona

C.evidence: Huge following but Camp Nou crowds are known as touristy and quiet outside big games; Grada d'Animació is the organised section. Camp Nou reopened in stages from Nov 2025 (same site, not a new stadium).

V.evidence: Catalan identity ('Més que un club'); member-owned with elected president; elite women's team (Femení); La Masia pathway (Yamal, Cubarsí, Fermín). Negreira referee-payments case and high tourist-oriented pricing hold it back. Spotify sponsor: no effect.

H.evidence: Global significance: Cruyff/total football legacy, 5 European Cups, La Masia influence on the game.

O.evidence: Member-owned (socis elect the president); conduct weaker: 'economic levers' (sold future TV-rights share to Sixth Street, etc.), heavy debt, governance turmoil; Laporta stood down in Feb 2026 ahead of elections.

S.evidence: Flick's high line and aggressive pressing since 2024.

adjustments.evidence: Founder and last-but-one backer; formally withdrew only in Feb 2026, leaving Real Madrid alone.
Repeated LaLiga squad-cost limit breaches and asset sales ('levers') to fund spending beyond income.

flags: 2026 presidential election outcome not verified; may affect O.
UEFA has fined the club for fan Nazi salutes (2023-24); not treated as an adjustment.

name: Bayern Munich

C.evidence: Allianz Arena (75,024) sells out; Südkurve (Schickeria, Club Nr. 12) is organised and active but the stadium is less intense overall than Germany's top atmospheres.

V.evidence: Member club (432,500 members) with low standing-ticket prices; strong women's team; fans protested Qatar Airways and the 'Visit Rwanda' deal, which Bayern scaled back in Aug 2025 into a youth-academy partnership. Residual Rwanda state tie keeps it from 8.

H.evidence: 6 European Cups, 35 German titles, the sextuple (2020); central to German football.

O.evidence: FC Bayern München e.V. holds the large majority of the AG (Adidas, Allianz, Audi minority stakes); 50+1 with members electing the president.

S.evidence: Kompany (since 2024) plays high-line, high-press attacking football; record 16 straight wins and 105 league goals by matchday 29 in 2025-26.

flags: Visit Rwanda: decide if the remaining Rwanda academy partnership should still count as an authoritarian-state sponsor.

name: Bodø/Glimt

C.evidence: Small but loyal crowd; Aspmyra (~8,270) is sold out and one of Europe's hardest away trips (Den Gule Horde, yellow rattles). City beaten 3-1 and Inter beaten there in 2025-26 UCL. 10,000-seat Arctic Arena under construction.

V.evidence: Northern Norwegian regional identity; community club with the 'Vårres Måte' development philosophy; local sponsor base, no betting shirt sponsor found; women's team exists.

H.evidence: 1975 Norwegian Cup (first northern club to win a national title); four league titles 2020-24; first Norwegian club in a European semi-final (Europa League 2025); 6-1 over Roma (2021).

O.evidence: Norwegian member association (members' club, no private owner found).

S.evidence: Knutsen's high-intensity, pressing possession game since 2018; a lasting club identity.

flags: Shirt sponsor and ownership detail not verified directly this session (Norwegian clubs are member associations).

name: Borussia Dortmund

C.evidence: Highest average attendance of any club worldwide in 81,365 Signal Iduna Park; the Yellow Wall (Südtribüne) is Europe's benchmark standing terrace.

V.evidence: Members' club with low ticket prices, anti-extremism fan statutes and Holocaust-remembrance work after a far-right (Borussenfront) past; members voted 556-247 against the Rheinmetall arms deal (non-binding) but it continues (-1 per rule); betting brands among commercial partners. Shirt sponsor Vodafone.

H.evidence: 8 German titles, 1997 Champions League, 1966 Cup Winners' Cup (first German European trophy); 2013 and 2024 UCL finals.

O.evidence: KGaA listed since 2000 but controlled by the e.V. (50+1); Evonik 7.8%, Signal Iduna 5.7%, Puma 5.1%. Members have a real voice (Rheinmetall vote).

S.evidence: Klopp-era gegenpress identity has faded; Kovač's side is more structured and pragmatic.

flags: Rheinmetall deal runs to 2027 unless ended early; re-check at expiry.

name: Club Brugge

C.evidence: Jan Breydel (29,062, shared with Cercle, athletics-era bowl) fills for big games; about 10,000 members in 62 fan clubs; the Blue Army section is loud. The number 12 is retired for supporters. New stadium planned since 2007, not built.

V.evidence: Main shirt sponsor Betsson (sports betting) since 2025 lowers; women's team in the Belgian Super League and a working academy (Club NXT) raise. Net slightly below typical.

H.evidence: Only Belgian club in a European Cup final (1978 v Liverpool); 1976 UEFA Cup final; 20 league titles and a record 12 cups.

O.evidence: President and main shareholder Bart Verhaeghe (property developer) since 2011; successful and stable, but he was named in the Belgian 'Clean Hands' football fraud investigation (outcome not verified here).

S.evidence: Well-coached, direct and energetic sides; no distinct pressing identity.

flags: Verhaeghe's status in the 'Clean Hands' case not verified this session; may lower O.

name: Como

C.evidence: Small crowds in the 13,602 Sinigaglia (1927 rationalist lakeside ground, strong character); ultras reorganised under 'Como 1907'; recent success has added tourists and celebrity visitors more than a big terrace culture.

V.evidence: Revolut shirt sponsor (no effect). Owners' spending built a largely imported squad (little local pathway); ticket prices rose sharply with Serie A/UCL (not verified in detail).

H.evidence: Serie A spells mainly in the 1980s; bankruptcies in 2004 and 2016 with fan-backed refoundings; first ever UCL qualification in 2026 (4th in 2025-26).

O.evidence: Owned since 2019 by Indonesia's Hartono brothers (Djarum group), among the world's richest; Henry and Fàbregas minority shareholders; stable but owner-funded model with no fan voice.

S.evidence: Fàbregas: possession-dominant, high-pressing, young technical side.

adjustments.evidence: Among Serie A's heaviest net spenders since promotion in 2024, funded by the Hartono fortune on a 13,600-seat revenue base.

flags: Hartono fortune rests on tobacco (Djarum): brief says no effect, confirm.
Spending figures not re-verified this session.

name: Feyenoord

C.evidence: Highest home attendance in Italy (San Siro ~75,800); the Curva Nord produces major choreographies and constant noise.
